versions.short: The bill would direct the Secretary of the Interior to award a grant of $6,000,000 each year for seven fiscal years to the National Law Enforcement Officers Memorial Fund, to be used for operating and expanding the programs of the National Law Enforcement Museum, subject to the availability of appropriations made in advance. The grant would support areas such as honoring fallen officers, public education about law enforcement history, officer safety and wellness training, community policing outreach, teacher programs, and collection and digital resources. As a condition of receiving the money, the Fund would have to offer free museum admission to active and retired officers and to family members of fallen officers, provide free general admission at least once a week, and undergo annual federal audits. The Fund would also have to report to the House and Senate natural resources committees on how the money was spent and what programs it delivered. The bill states that it does not authorize any additional funds beyond those appropriated in advance.
